decision_rule: remove CP4 and CP7 if every registered coverage requirement holds without them with acceptable support; otherwise rewrite the ambiguous wordings, invalidate every row generated under them and regenerate before recomputing coverage

CP4.why: the wording states q as a target and names no bound, so it does not distinguish the registered predicate (100*S/W >= q) from the reading that takes q as exact; the two disagree on every answer past q, which the verifier scores as a pass
CP4.wordings: Give {q} percent of words doubled letters. / Make {q} percent of words carry doubled letters.

CP7.why: the wording states q as a target and names no bound, so it does not distinguish the registered predicate (100*S/W >= q) from the reading that takes q as exact; the two disagree on every answer past q, which the verifier scores as a pass
CP7.wordings: Give {q} percent of words letter a. / Make {q} percent of words carry letter a.

leave_one_family_out_finding: coverage is NOT robust to dropping an arbitrary eligible reference family on three of the four replications. C4 requires four well-formed straddling feature groups and three models have exactly four, so any one of them is load-bearing. This is a property of the reference pool that v4r3 already had: the sweep run on v4r3's population returns the same families. It is reported, not repaired, because repairing it would mean adding candidate families after seeing a coverage result, which §12.6 forbids outside its registered expansion --- and the registered expansion draws from the frozen reserve, which is available if the researcher decides the margin is too thin

C1_bracketed.rule: an eligible reference rung strictly below iota_A and one strictly above

C2_groups_per_side.rule: at least 3 eligible reference FEATURE GROUPS on each side of iota_A

C3_near_density.rule: at least 6 eligible rungs within 0.15 of iota_A, from at least 3 feature groups

C4_straddling_families.rule: at least 4 reference families straddle iota_A with at least 3 eligible rungs spanning 0.40 in iota, from that many distinct feature groups

C5_total_points.rule: at least 12 eligible reference rungs in total

C6_shortlist_feasible.rule: at least 6 eligible reference families, from at least 4 feature groups, so §12.3's shortlist is not short before it starts

C7_class_matched.rule: at least one eligible class rung within 0.15 of iota_A. NOT terminal: an unmatched class companion attaches COMPANION_CLASS_NOT_MATCHED and the study proceeds

not_chosen_for_cost: the rule above is prospective and reads coverage only. The cost comparison is recorded because it is a real difference between the two remedies and a reader is entitled to see it, not because it entered the decision
reads: the §12.2 pre-screen difficulty table on each v4r3 REGIME_SCREEN record: solo compliance, chance compliance and solo vacuity per rung
what_removal_costs: CP4 and CP7 were the only families carrying the rate-lower-bound form. The class arm becomes {count lower bound, exact count}. §7.4-R3's own argument is why that is tolerable: A is an exact-count production constraint and CX1 is A's rule over a different marker word, which is the tightest class companion the grammar can build. The removed families were the loosest
what_rewriting_would_have_cost: the four wordings render at 60 severities across CP4 and CP7's declared ranges. Changing a live wording invalidates every measurement taken under it, and the §12.2 screen spreads four wordings over its 24 pre-screen topics, so the whole of both families' measured rows --- 16 round-0 rungs x 24 topics on each of four replications, 1,536 generations --- would have to be regenerated, not only the 768 rows carrying the two defective wordings
why_c1_to_c6_cannot_move: §12.6's first six conditions read rows whose role is `reference`. CP4 and CP7 are `class_control`, so their removal cannot change those six on any table. This is a property of the criterion, not an observation about these four models, and the run below confirms it rather than resting on it
